excerpt: Easily upload PDFs, websites, YouTube videos, audio files, Google Docs, or Google Slides or discover new sources.
Chat with your notebook to get grounded information based on your sources with clear in-line citations for accuracy, transparency, and trust.
Transform your sources into approachable formats such as study guides, briefings, audio overviews, mind maps, and more.
Each source can contain up to 500,000 words or up to 200MB for uploaded files.
Find an auto-generated summary of the entire source in the Source Guide.
You can hover over any citation to get the full quoted text right away.
Custom: Best for choosing a specific style ("Respond like a PhD student") or suggesting a role ("Pretend to be a role-playing game host.").
You can make your notebook public and share a link with anyone with a Google account.
Owners of public notebooks with paid subscriptions can view usage analytics in the analytics tab.
Listen to Audio Overviews on the go and download them for offline playback.
Share content directly to Gemini Notebook when viewing a website, PDF, or YouTube video on your device.
To convert a single note to a source: Open the note. Select Convert to source.
You can export your notes to Google Docs or Google Sheets.
Mind Maps in Gemini Notebook visually summarize your uploaded sources, showing main topics and related ideas as a branching diagram.
Choose a format. Deep Dive (default) for an in-depth conversation. Two hosts unpack and connect topics from your sources in a lively conversation.
Video Overviews transform the sources in your notebook into an engaging video.
Flashcards or Quizzes help you master your material by turning information from your sources into interactive study aids.
Infographics turn complex information from your sources into a single, engaging visual summary.
Transform your sources into a polished presentation by generating a Slide Deck, perfect for sharing or reviewing key concepts.
For Workspace and Workspace for Education users, Gemini Notebook is now a core service (like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Docs).
If you select a citation, Gemini Notebook automatically navigates to the location of the quote, so you can easily view it in context.
Select a conversational style. Default: Best for general purpose research and brainstorming tasks.
Audio Overviews are deep-dive discussions between AI hosts that provide in-depth summaries of the key topics in your uploaded sources.

Video Overviews transform the sources in your notebook into an engaging video. They distill complex information into clear, digestible content, providing a comprehensive and engaging visual deep dive of your material.
Transform your sources into a polished presentation by generating a Slide Deck, perfect for sharing or reviewing key concepts. Present your deck instantly in Gemini Notebook or share it as a PDF.
You can use notes to capture and organize information, identify key insights and interpretations from your sources, and add your own thoughts.
Create your own, or choose from FAQ, study guide, briefing document, or an AI suggested report type.
Get insights in the moment by asking questions about your sources.
Select which sources in your notebook the model should use to answer your questions.
Best for choosing a specific style ("Respond like a PhD student”) or suggesting a role ("Pretend to be a role-playing game host.")
To get the full quoted text, hover over any citation. To navigate directly to the quote and review it in context, select a citation.
Select a conversational style. Default: Best for general purpose research and brainstorming tasks... Custom: Best for choosing a specific style
To pin Gemini Notebook chat responses to the noteboard for your reference later, select Save to note.
Choose a format. Deep Dive (default) for an in-depth conversation... The Brief for a quick overview... The Debate for exploring multiple perspectives.
Get insights in the moment by asking questions about your sources. Listen to Audio Overviews on the go and download them for offline playback.

Play Books: Add eligible ebooks from Google Play as sources in Gemini Notebook. At this time, only text is supported.
To chat with a specific set of sources in your Notebook, select them individually in the “Source” panel.
To navigate directly to the quote and review it in context, select a citation.
Custom: Best for choosing a specific style ("Respond like a PhD student”) or suggesting a role ("Pretend to be a role-playing game host.").
When you save a response as a note, the original format—including tables and clickable inline citations—gets saved.
Created notes automatically appear in the Sources panel alongside your uploaded sources. This means your notes can be used for Q&A, cited in Chat responses, and included in artifact generation.
Select nodes to ask questions: Directly select a node in the Mind Map to ask questions in the Gemini Notebook chat about that specific topic.
The Critique for critical feedback. Two hosts provide a constructive evaluation of material like an essay or design doc.
Select the difficulty: Choose between easy, medium, and hard.
Download your flashcards as a CSV file.
Choose a visual style (only for 18+ users), such as Sketch Note, Kawaii, Professional, etc.
Use the three dots menu next to your generated Infographic to rename, download as a PNG file, share, or delete.
When you are out of AI limits, you can now delay generations for later.

NotebookLM is pretty cool since it can hold a ton of context, but it falls far below reasonable expectations of Google. The user downgraded their Gemini subscription and switched to Claude, calling it much better.
NotebookLM is genuinely useful for structured research workflows. This user's concern is not the name but whether the 'notebook' metaphor survives the rebrand.
Wants audio overviews of scientific papers to 'read' while driving. NotebookLM/Gemini Notebook sort of does this, but the two-person podcast format is kind of annoying and it can't pronounce math.
Has been using NotebookLM for studying and really likes it. Feels the new name reflects the product better.

Listening to the podcasts was interesting at first, but the novelty wore off. The interactive mode for talking with the podcasters was 'janky as hell.' Switched to ChatGPT Live for audio learning: drops in a paper link on walks, has it explain the content in small nuggets, and asks for Socratic-style quizzing.
Not a big deal to be honest. Still works just as great.
My problem with NotebookLM was that you had to give it URLs or docs, you couldn't just have it search for docs and then incorporate them into your research.

Used it while driving to listen to high-level walkthroughs of code: Plan 9 C ed and Karpathy's toy LLM in C, then read the source afterward. Hearing it explain Ken Thompson's bit-stealing trick was enlightening, and as a non-C programmer the bird's-eye view first was useful.

Calls it a well-designed product but wishes pulling in emails were easier. For one notebook, they had to use gyb and mhonarc to retrieve Gmail messages, convert them to text, and split them in a way the Notebook would accept.
Notes that the product has been integrated into the Gemini web page, where it now appears on the left above recent chats.
